title: Courses kept offline
summary: A switch on a course that downloads all of its audio and pictures and keeps them downloaded as it grows.
description:
A learner who is about to be without a connection (a flight, a trip abroad) wants a course that simply works. Audio and pictures are otherwise made the first time a lesson needs them, which takes the network and the learner's key.

Keeping a course offline makes the app fetch everything its lessons play and show ahead of time, and say plainly what will still need a connection. Songs and Wikipedia sources are stored when they are made, so they are there already.

requirements.text: A course can be marked to be kept offline with a switch on its page; no course is marked until the learner does so.
Switching it on starts downloading everything the course lacks: the audio of everything its lessons say and every picture they show.

The audio counted for a course is every word, sentence and dialogue line of its lessons, a story's sentences in each speaker's voice, a scene's sentences, each word's near neighbour by sound, and the built-in sound pairs for the sounds its words have.
The pictures counted for a course are the words of its picture lessons, each scene, and each panel of its stories.
A course is ready offline when every counted clip and picture is stored; its page shows how many of each are downloaded.
A course that gains content after it was ready is no longer shown as ready until the new audio and pictures are stored.
For courses kept offline, missing audio is fetched by itself at startup and after the tutor adds to a course.

Pictures are drawn for a course kept offline only when the learner switches it on or taps Download now, which also tries again the pictures that failed before; by itself the app leaves a lesson's pictures to the device that made the lesson.
The page says how many of the course's lessons are conversations, which need a connection whatever is downloaded.
Without an OpenRouter key nothing is downloaded, and the page says a key is needed.
Switching it off deletes nothing that was downloaded.
The mark syncs with the course, and what was downloaded syncs as files, so a course made ready on one device is ready on the others once they have synced.
A course is downloaded once at a time: asking again while a download runs starts no second one.
While a course downloads on Android, the app is kept alive with a quiet notification.

questions: At startup, two synced devices that both keep a course offline can each fetch the same missing clip before they sync. Speech is cheap and the copies settle to one, but should only one device fetch?

Example sentences shown after a wrong answer are made by a model the first time and are not downloaded ahead; offline, sentences from the learner's own courses stand in. Should a course kept offline have them made ahead too?
Slow versions of a line are still made only when asked for. Should a course kept offline include them?
